scope: current-shell object geometry, selection keyboard, grouping/z-order readiness, and semantic clipboard reachability

rows.chaptera: Direct page-local movable objects begin a MoveTransaction on primary drag, update transient preview bounds during pointer motion, and commit one move on drag stop.
rows.publisher: A selected object or group can be repositioned by dragging it.
rows.notes: Ordinary drag law matches at the user-interaction level. Exact snap/threshold policy is not inferred from Publisher.

rows.chaptera: Current canvas drag path does not consume Shift as a movement constraint; it feeds pointer coordinates directly to MoveTransaction.
chaptera_evidence: full current-file audit: no Shift constraint in object MoveTransaction canvas route
rows.publisher: Holding Shift while dragging constrains object movement to a straight line.
rows.notes: Reuse the existing owner. Exact axis choice/tie/mid-drag transition remains with the bounded discriminator rather than being guessed.

rows.chaptera: Eight visible resize handles admit a ResizeTransaction, render a transient preview and commit one ResizeNode-style change on drag stop.
rows.publisher: Selected objects expose sizing handles that resize the object when dragged.
rows.notes: Match is limited to ordinary handle-drag resizing; object-specific picture constraints remain capability-gated.

rows.chaptera: Current ordinary-object canvas resize route does not feed Ctrl/Shift modifier state into the resize transaction.
chaptera_evidence: main.rs:3015 only reads Ctrl for zoom; no resize-modifier routing in canvas gesture
rows.publisher: Ctrl while dragging keeps the object center fixed; Shift on a corner handle preserves proportions; Ctrl+Shift combines both behaviors.
rows.notes: The deterministic geometry law is already owned by INTERACTION-RESIZE-CONSTRAINTS-01. No duplicate modifier model is created.

rows.chaptera: SceneSelectionState stores a set and primary item, but the reachable canvas click/drag path currently finishes through select_only(), which clears the set before inserting one instance.
rows.publisher: Publisher documents selecting multiple objects by holding Shift while selecting additional objects; grouped-object guidance also uses Shift-click selection.
rows.notes: Historical/canonical multi-selection semantics already exist; this row is shell restoration, not a new selection model.

rows.chaptera: The current top-level update path exposes Ctrl+O but no canvas Arrow-key object-nudge route. ArrowLeft/ArrowRight handling in process_canvas_text_input belongs to Story caret/selection.
rows.publisher: Arrow keys nudge a selected object; Publisher also documents an Alt+Arrow object-move escape hatch when the insertion cursor is inside the selected text object.
rows.notes: Current collision-safe bridge is already restoring the closed nudge/focus law; do not add another keyboard router.

rows.chaptera: Current shell has no reachable canvas Ctrl/Cmd+A object Select All route; Ctrl/Cmd+A seen in GUI tests targets a multiline text widget rather than canonical canvas selection.
chaptera_evidence: GUI test around main.rs:5317-5332 exercises multiline text input Ctrl+A, not canvas object selection
rows.publisher: Ctrl+A selects all objects on the page when focus is not inside a text box; with insertion focus in a text box it selects Story text.
rows.notes: The existing restore owner explicitly owns the Story-vs-canvas focus split.

rows.chaptera: Escape is currently handled inside active Story text mode to exit text editing, but there is no final top-level canvas fallback that clears object selection.
rows.publisher: Publisher documents Escape clearing a selected object/selection, with deeper context-specific Escape behavior handled by focus.
rows.notes: Reuse current routing bridge and existing Escape precedence law; no second tool/focus model.

rows.chaptera: Current main has no reachable authored Group/Ungroup command in the desktop shell.
chaptera_evidence: current main.rs full-file interaction audit: no Group/Ungroup command route
rows.publisher: Publisher exposes Group/Ungroup for selected objects and documents multi-object selection before grouping; Ctrl+Shift+G is the keyboard route.
rows.notes: This is an admitted-but-not-shipped capability, not a regression from a closed shell feature. Non-contiguous authored grouping already has EDITOR-AUTHORED-GROUP-SET-UI-01.

rows.chaptera: Current scene hit testing uses z_order/paint_order to choose the topmost object, but current main exposes no authored Bring/Send mutation command.
chaptera_evidence: current main.rs full-file interaction audit: no authored Bring/Send command route
rows.publisher: Publisher exposes Bring to Front, Send to Back, Bring Forward and Send Backward; keyboard aliases include Alt+F6 / Alt+Shift+F6.
rows.notes: Authored stacking semantics already have their own authority chain. Hit-test paint order is not treated as authoring authority.

rows.chaptera: Current shell has no canonical focus/capability router for Ctrl/Cmd+C/X/V across selected Story text versus selected document objects.
chaptera_evidence: main.rs:1686-1703 exposes search-result text copy conveniences only
rows.publisher: Publisher documents Copy, Cut and Paste over selected text or objects, including Ctrl+C/Ctrl+X/Ctrl+V and legacy Insert/Delete aliases.
rows.notes: Base semantic clipboard routing already owns the focus split; object-set and Story-range extensions have separate existing owners.

rows.chaptera: Search results expose Copy match and Copy full story buttons that place recovered text on the OS clipboard.
rows.publisher: No exact Publisher analogue is required for this Chaptera recovery/search convenience.
rows.notes: Do not misclassify these buttons as semantic document object/text editing clipboard parity.
